sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Eithne of Tara, called Tháebfhota or Long-Sides, was daughter of King Cathaír Mór. She wed several kings of Tara, among them Conn of the Hundred Battles and his grandson Cormac Mac Airt. She bore Cormac a son, Cairbre Lifechair. While she reigned, the fields bore three crops each year. This marks her as a form of the sovereignty goddess.
